central_claim: The exact analytical solution for multi-reference RLHF (both RKL and FKL objectives) outperforms both single reference approaches and the MRPO approximation, achieving a 66.1% win rate when combining both references.
claim_evidence: Abstract states 'This paper presents the first exact solution to the multiple reference model problem in reverse KL-regularized RLHF.' Figure 1 shows both online and offline experiments where exact analytical RKL objective outperforms MRPO approximation and single reference objective. Table 1 shows DPO with both references achieves 66.1% win rate vs 56.4% (single reference SFT model) vs 59.8% (single reference 14B model).
mre_config: Offline DPO training with Qwen 2.5 0.5B-Instruct on UltraFeedback dataset, using two reference models (Qwen 2.5 0.5B-Instruct + Qwen 2.5 1.5B-Instruct) with geometric ensemble (alpha=0.5), RKL objective, gamma=1.0, per_device_train_batch_size=2, gradient_accumulation_steps=16, 1 epoch.

central_claim: Antidistillation sampling modifies a language model's next-token probability distribution to generate reasoning traces that resist model distillation while preserving the original model's utility.
claim_evidence: Abstract: 'By strategically modifying a model's next-token probability distribution, antidistillation sampling poisons reasoning traces, rendering them significantly less effective for distillation while preserving the model's utility.' Figure 3 (GSM8K): With similar teacher accuracy reduction (~4%), temperature sampling yields distilled student accuracy ~52% while antidistillation sampling reduces it to ~40%.
mre_config: On GSM8K, use DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B as teacher, Qwen2.5-3B as proxy student, and Llama-3.2-3B as student. Generate holdout traces (70/30 train/holdout split), compute proxy student gradients via save_grad.py, generate training traces with gentraces.py at lambda=0 (baseline) and lambda~0.15 (antidistillation), distill student models via distill.py with LoRA rank 128, 3 epochs, then evaluate accuracy on GSM8K Platinum test set.

code_available.evidence: GitHub repo locuslab/antidistillation-sampling verified with complete pipeline: gentraces.py (trace generation with antidistillation), save_grad.py (gradient computation), distill.py (student distillation), utils.py (dataset loading), gen_config.yaml, train_config.yaml, acc_config.yaml, pipeline.sh. README documents installation and quick start.

dataset_available.evidence: GSM8K benchmark is standard public dataset (openai/gsm8k on HuggingFace, MIT license). OpenReview supplement contains complete pipeline code with dataset loading functions for GSM8K, MATH, and MMLU.

agent_task: Reproduce the core antidistillation sampling result on GSM8K: (1) Generate holdout reasoning traces using DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B teacher on 30% of GSM8K training data with gentraces.py. central_claim: RADiAnce significantly outperforms baseline models on protein binder design tasks, achieving higher amino acid recovery (AAR), lower RMSD, better binding affinity (ΔΔG), and improved interaction pattern recovery (ISM) for both antibody CDR and peptide sequence-structure co-design.
claim_evidence: Abstract states 'Extensive experiments show that RADiAnce significantly outperforms baseline models across multiple metrics, including binding affinity and recovery of geometries and interactions.' Table 2 (tab:peptide_result) and Table 3 (table:antibody_result) report the main results showing RADiAnce achieves 39.42% AAR, 2.29 RMSD, 1.963 kJ/mol ΔΔG, 41.94% IMP, 52.15% ISM on peptide task versus UniMoMo's 38.69%, 2.31, 2.409, 40.86%, 49.13%; and 54.66% AAR, 0.9443 RMSD, -6.236 kJ/mol ΔΔG, 71.67% IMP, 71.64% ISM on HCDR3 task versus UniMoMo's 52.34%, 1.040, -7.438, 65.00%, 71.52%.
mre_config: Full RADiAnce training pipeline on peptide task: (1) Train Contrastive VAE on cross-domain data (peptide+antibody+ProtFrag) following configs/contrastive/train_pt.yaml using 8 GPUs; (2) Compute RAG top-k database using cal_topk.py with trained CVAE checkpoint; (3) Train Latent Diffusion Model following configs/LDM-rag/train_pt.yaml using 8 GPUs; (4) Generate 100 samples per test complex on LNR benchmark using generate.py with configs/test/test_pep.yaml; (5) Evaluate ISM metric (Interaction Site Match) against ground truth.

central_claim: GVM (Gradient Variance Minimization) achieves 2-4x convergence speedup and improved final accuracy over vanilla RAFT++ for chain-of-thought reasoning fine-tuning on mathematical reasoning tasks.
claim_evidence: Abstract states 'achieves a 2-4× speedup and considerable accuracy improvements over vanilla RAFT.' Table 1 (Section 5, Main Results) shows GVM-RAFT++ with iter=13 achieves 71.55% on Math500 vs RAFT++ at 69.02%. Figure 2 (Section 5, ablation) shows ~2x speedup in update steps for N'=8 configuration on Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B.

Training runs 10 iterations with 9 gradient steps each, batch size 1024, learning rate 1e-6, alpha=0.001, beta=2.0.

central_claim: EF-3DGS integrates event cameras with 3DGS for free-trajectory scene reconstruction, achieving up to 3dB higher PSNR and 40% lower ATE compared to state-of-the-art methods in high-speed/low-frame-rate scenarios.
claim_evidence: Abstract states: 'Our method achieves up to 3dB higher PSNR and 40% lower Absolute Trajectory Error (ATE) compared to state-of-the-art methods under challenging high-speed scenarios.' Table 1 (Tanks and Temples PSNR results) and Table 2 (pose accuracy) report these headline results at 1 FPS.
mre_config: Test EF-3DGS on a single Tanks and Temples scene (e.g., Auditorium or Train) at 1 FPS frame rate using event-frame hybrid input. The MRE evaluates novel view synthesis (PSNR, SSIM, LPIPS) and pose estimation (ATE, RPE) metrics. Training requires: (1) event synthesis via V2E simulator after RIFE upsampling, (2) joint pose-scene optimization with N=6 event subintervals over 50 frames, (3) Fixed-GS two-stage color refinement. Target metrics: ~24 PSNR, ~0.38 ATE (vs CF-3DGS baseline of ~20.5 PSNR, ~0.90 ATE).

code_available.evidence: No GitHub repository found for EF-3DGS after exhaustive searches including: full title 'EF-3DGS Event-Aided Free-Trajectory 3D Gaussian Splatting', arXiv ID '2410.15392', method/acronym variants 'EF-3DGS' alone, 'event-aided 3DGS', 'free-trajectory 3DGS', and related terms. HuggingFace search also returned no results for EF-3DGS. The paper's NeurIPS checklist explicitly states: 'Our source code and the self-collect dataset will be openly accessible after the paper is accepted.' Event-3DGS (a related but different method) exists at github.com/lanpokn/Event-3DGS but cannot reproduce EF-3DGS.

dataset_available.evidence: Tanks and Temples benchmark is publicly available at tanksandtemples.org with downloadable image sets, videos, ground truth geometry, and Python downloader script. The paper uses this standard benchmark (SIGGRAPH 2017) for evaluation across 9 scenes.

weights_available.evidence: No pretrained model weights or checkpoints found. OpenReview supplement only contains one file: EF_3DGS_supp_video_.mp4 (a demo video). No checkpoint, weights, or model files are bundled or publicly released.

dataset_is_standard.evidence: Tanks and Temples is a widely recognized 3D reconstruction benchmark published at SIGGRAPH 2017 with publicly available ground truth data from laser scanning and established evaluation protocol. It is commonly used as a standard benchmark in 3D reconstruction research.

agent_task: Reproduce the central claim by: (1) Download the Tanks and Temples Auditorium scene from tanksandtemples.org (video or image set), (2) Generate synthetic event data using V2E simulator as described in paper: 'we upsample original videos by RIFE and then apply the simulator V2E', (3) Implement EF-3DGS from scratch with all components: EGM loss for event-frame fusion, LEGM/CMax for pose optimization (r=3, λcm=0.1, λgrad=0.2), PBA for cross-view consistency (λPBA=0.5), and Fixed-GS two-stage training (4:1 ratio), (4) Train on 1 FPS downsampled data with N=6 event subintervals over 50 frames on a single scene, (5) Evaluate novel view synthesis (PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS) and pose estimation (ATE/RPE) metrics.
